segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In public discussion of business, we take certain values for granted.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Today I’m going to talk about four of them: collaboration, hard work, creativity and excellence.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Most people would say they’re all ‘good things’.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I’m going to suggest that’s an over-simple view.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The trouble with these values is that they’re theoretical concepts, removed from the reality of day-to-day business.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Pursue values by all means, but be prepared for what may happen as a result.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They can actually cause damage, which is not at all the intention. [[ ]] Business leaders generally try to do the right thing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But all too often the right thing backfires, if those leaders adopt values without understanding and managing the side effects that arise [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The values can easily get in the way of what’s actually intended.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So the first value I’m going to discuss is collaboration.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Er, let me give you an example.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: On a management training course I once attended, we were put into groups and had to construct a bridge across a stream [[ ]] , using building blocks that we were given.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The rule was that everyone in the team had to move at least one building block during the construction.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This was intended to encourage teamwork.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But it was really a job best done by one person.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The other teams tried to collaborate on building the structure, and descended into confusion [[ ]] , with everyone getting in each other’s way.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Our team leader solved the challenge brilliantly.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: She simply asked everyone in the team to move a piece a few centimetres, to comply with the rule, and then let the person in the team with an aptitude for puzzles like this build it alone.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We finished before any other team.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My point is that the task wasn’t really suited to teamworking, so why make it one?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Teamwork can also lead to inconsistency – a common cause of poor sales.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In the case of a smartphone that a certain company launched, one director wanted to target the business market, and another demanded it was aimed at consumers.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The company wanted both directors to be involved, so gave the product a consumer-friendly name, but marketed it to companies.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The result was that it met the needs of neither group.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It would have been better to let one director or the other have his way, not both. [[ ]] Now industriousness, or hard work.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s easy to mock people who say they work hard: after all, a hamster running around in a wheel is working hard – and getting nowhere.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Of course hard work is valuable, but only when properly targeted.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Otherwise it wastes the resources that companies value most – time and energy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And that’s bad for the organisation. [[ ]] There’s a management model that groups people according to four criteria: clever, hard-working, stupid and lazy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Here ‘lazy’ means having a rational determination not to carry out unnecessary tasks [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It doesn’t mean trying to avoid work altogether.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Most people display two of these characteristics, and the most valuable people are those who are both clever and lazy: they possess intellectual clarity, and they don’t rush into making decisions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They come up with solutions to save the time and energy spent by the stupid and hard-working group.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Instead of throwing more man-hours at a problem, the clever and lazy group looks for a more effective solution.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Next we come to creativity.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This often works well – creating an attention-grabbing TV commercial, for example, might lead to increased sales.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But it isn’t always a good thing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Some advertising campaigns are remembered for their creativity, without having any effect on sales.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This happened a few years ago with the launch of a chocolate bar: subsequent research showed that plenty of consumers remembered the adverts, but had no idea what was being advertised [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The trouble is that the creator derives pleasure from coming up with the idea, and wrongly assumes the audience for the campaign will share that feeling.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A company that brings out thousands of new products may seem more creative than a company that only has a few, but it may be too creative, and make smaller profits.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Creativity needs to be targeted, to solve a problem that the company has identified [[ ]] .

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Just coming up with more and more novel products isn’t necessarily a good thing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And finally, excellence.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We all know companies that claim they ‘strive for excellence’, but it takes a long time to achieve excellence.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In business, being first with a product is more profitable than having the best product.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A major study of company performance compared pioneers – that is, companies bringing out the first version of a particular product – with followers, the companies that copied and improved on that product.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The study found that the pioneers commanded an average market share of 29 percent, while the followers achieved less than half that, only 13 percent [[ ]] – even though their product might have been better.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Insisting on excellence in everything we do is time-consuming, wastes energy and leads to losing out on opportunities.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Sometimes, second-rate work is more worthwhile than excellence. ‘Make sure it’s excellent’ sounds like a good approach to business, but the ‘just-get-started’ approach is likely to be more successful.
